stories.headline: Alibaba Releases Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, an Open-Weight MoE Model That Rivals Dense Models 10x Its Active Size

key_facts.fact: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is a sparse MoE model with 35B total parameters but only 3B active per token (256 experts, 8+1 activated per layer), reducing compute by ~90% versus dense architecture.
Scores 73.4% on SWE-bench Verified, beating Google's Gemma4-31B by 21.4 points. On Terminal-Bench 2.0, it scores 51.5% vs Gemma4-31B's 42.9%.
Released under Apache 2.0 license with no usage restrictions. A quantized 21GB version runs on consumer hardware like an RTX 4090 or M5 MacBook.
Natively multimodal, supporting text, image, and video inputs. Processes hour-long videos with up to 224K video tokens and scored 83.7% on VideoMMU, highest in its class.
Introduces a 'thinking preservation' option to retain reasoning context from historical messages, improving multi-turn agentic workflows.

stories.headline: Anthropic Ships Claude Opus 4.7 With 87.6% SWE-bench Verified, New xhigh Effort Level

key_facts.fact: SWE-bench Verified jumps from 80.8% (Opus 4.6) to 87.6%, and SWE-bench Pro from 53.4% to 64.3%, putting Opus 4.7 ahead of GPT-5.4 (57.7%) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (54.2%) on multi-language coding tasks.
Opus 4.7 introduces a new 'xhigh' effort level between high and max, now the default in Claude Code for all plans, plus 3x vision resolution upgrade to 3.75 megapixels (2,576px long edge).
Tool use leads all models on MCP-Atlas at 77.3%, and computer use (OSWorld-Verified) climbs from 72.7% to 78.0%, ahead of GPT-5.4 (75.0%).
Pricing unchanged at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens. Available via Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.
Anthropic explicitly states Opus 4.7 is 'less broadly capable' than Claude Mythos Preview, which leads on most benchmarks including 93.9% on SWE-bench Verified.
Cursor reported a jump from 58% to 70% on CursorBench, and Rakuten reported 3x more production task resolutions than on Opus 4.6.

stories.headline: ASML Raises 2026 Revenue Guidance to €36-40B as AI Chip Demand Overwhelms Supply

key_facts.fact: ASML raised its 2026 sales forecast to between €36 billion and €40 billion, up from the previous guidance of €34-39 billion, a 4% increase.
Q1 2026 net revenue was €8.8 billion, above the market consensus of €8.5 billion. Net income was €2.8 billion, above the expected €2.5 billion.
ASML is expected to deliver 80 EUV machines in 2026, each costing approximately $230 million, up from 60 machines projected earlier.
CEO Christoph Fouquet cited AI infrastructure investment as the key driver, saying chip demand is outpacing supply and customers are accelerating capacity expansion plans.
Multiple analysts raised price targets: Berenberg to €1,570, Deutsche Bank to €1,600, and Citi to €1,675, all maintaining buy ratings.

stories.headline: Blue Origin Static Fires Reused New Glenn Booster, Targeting Historic First Reflight on April 19

key_facts.fact: Blue Origin completed a successful 19-second static fire of a previously flown New Glenn first-stage booster on April 16 at Cape Canaveral, clearing a critical hurdle before the rocket's first booster reuse attempt.

The NG-3 launch is targeted for April 19, carrying AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to LEO. It will be New Glenn's third mission and the first to fly a reused booster, nicknamed 'Never Tell Me The Odds.'

Blue Origin replaced all seven BE-4 engines during refurbishment but kept the outer structure from the NG-2 ESCAPADE mission. The NG-2 engines will be reused on future flights once engineers assess full reuse economics.
BlueBird 7 features a nearly 2,400-square-foot phased-array antenna — one of the largest communication arrays ever deployed in LEO — and will beam broadband directly to unmodified cellphones.

stories.headline: China Q1 GDP Beats Expectations at 5.0%, but March Export Slump Signals Iran War Drag Ahead

key_facts.fact: China's GDP grew 5.0% year-on-year in Q1 2026, beating the 4.8% consensus forecast and accelerating from 4.5% in Q4 2025 — the first major economy to report since the Iran war began on February 28.

March industrial output rose 5.7% YoY (vs 5.5% forecast), but retail sales disappointed at just 1.7% YoY (vs 2.3% expected) and fixed asset investment grew only 1.7% YoY. Property investment fell 11.2% YoY.
Export growth plunged from 21.8% YoY in January-February to just 2.5% in March as the Iran war disrupted shipping and raised logistics costs. For Q1 overall, exports still grew 14.7%.

NBS warned of 'complex and volatile' external conditions. Beijing in March set a GDP growth target of 4.5–5.0% — the lowest in decades. China's factory-gate PPI turned positive for the first time since September 2022.

organizations: National Bureau of Statistics of China

stories.headline: Factory Raises $150M Series C at $1.5B Valuation for Model-Agnostic AI Coding Agents

key_facts.fact: Factory raised $150 million in Series C funding at a $1.5 billion valuation, led by Khosla Ventures with participation from Sequoia Capital, Insight Partners, and Blackstone.

Factory's key differentiator is switching between different foundation models (Anthropic's Claude, DeepSeek, etc.) depending on task complexity. Its Droid product is used daily by hundreds of thousands of developers.
Enterprise customers include Morgan Stanley, Ernst & Young, Palo Alto Networks, NVIDIA, and Adobe. Revenue has doubled month-over-month for six consecutive months.

Use cases extend beyond code completion to include COBOL migration, legacy technical debt cleanup, and end-to-end automation from ticket to PR. New 'Missions' system supports long-duration multi-agent collaboration.
Founded in 2023 by Matan Grinberg, a UC Berkeley PhD dropout who cold-emailed Sequoia's Shaun Maguire. Engineering team grew from 17 to 27 while valuation grew 10x.

stories.headline: Google-Backed Venture Sells Record $5.7B Junk Bond to Build Two Indiana AI Data Centers

key_facts.fact: Data centers linked to Alphabet's Google are seeking to raise $5.7 billion from a junk-bond sale, the largest US dollar junk bond ever to finance the AI buildout boom.
Morgan Stanley kicked off marketing on Wednesday (April 15) and is expected to price the notes as soon as this week. The proceeds will fund two data centers on a campus in Sullivan County, Indiana.
The data centers will be leased to cloud-compute startup FluidStack and backstopped by Google. The JV issuing the bonds is called Meridian Arc HoldCo, owned by Next Frontier and FluidStack.

FluidStack recently announced a $50 billion deal with Anthropic to build custom data centers and is in talks to raise $1 billion at an $18 billion valuation led by Jane Street and Situational Awareness.

stories.headline: IEA Chief Warns Europe Has 'Maybe Six Weeks' of Jet Fuel Left as Hormuz Crisis Deepens

key_facts.fact: IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said in an AP interview on April 16 that Europe has 'maybe six weeks or so' of jet fuel remaining, calling it 'the largest energy crisis we have ever faced.'

More than 110 oil-laden tankers and over 15 LNG carriers are stranded in the Persian Gulf waiting to transit the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed since the Iran war started on February 28.
Over 80 key energy assets in the region have been damaged during the war, with more than one-third severely damaged. Birol said full recovery could take up to two years even after a peace deal.

Airports in northern Italy (Milan-Linate, Venice, Treviso, Bologna) are already rationing jet fuel for short-haul flights. Airports Council International Europe warned the European Commission that shortages could begin in early May.
US jet fuel prices have surged to $4.69/gallon from $2.50 before the war. TotalEnergies has warned that if Gulf supplies remain blocked in June, it would not be able to supply all customers.

stories.headline: Israel and Lebanon Begin 10-Day Ceasefire Brokered by US, Boosting Broader Iran Peace Hopes

key_facts.fact: The ceasefire took effect on April 16, 2026 at 17:00 EST (midnight Beirut time), announced by Trump after separate calls with Israeli PM Netanyahu and Lebanese President Aoun.
Under the agreement, Israel will not carry out offensive military operations against Lebanese targets but preserves the right to self-defense against 'planned, imminent, or ongoing attacks.'

Netanyahu said Israeli troops will not withdraw and will maintain a 10-km 'security zone' inside southern Lebanon. Hezbollah, not a formal party to the deal, said Israel's occupation 'grants Lebanon and its people the right to resist it.'

Iran had linked further US-Iran talks to a ceasefire in Lebanon. The current US-Iran ceasefire is set to expire in six days. Trump invited both Netanyahu and Lebanese President Aoun to the White House for further talks.
Over 1 million people remain displaced by the war in Lebanon. The war between Israel and Hezbollah has killed more than 2,100 in Lebanon and 23 in Israel since it intensified.

stories.headline: Japan Joins US-Philippines Balikatan Military Drills With 17,000 Troops in First Large-Scale Role

key_facts.fact: Japan will participate at large scale in the annual US-Philippines Balikatan ('shoulder-to-shoulder') exercises for the first time, running from April 20 to May 8 with over 17,000 troops across air, land, sea, cyber, and space domains.
Analysts say Japan's expanded role reflects its growing focus on Taiwan's defense: 'Tokyo considers this as related to Taiwan's defense,' said retired US Marine Grant Newsham.

China continues to tighten control of the South China Sea and is using ships and a floating barrier to block access to Scarborough Shoal, 220 km west of the Philippine island of Luzon, according to satellite imagery reported by Bild.

Japan's participation is enabled by the Japan-Philippines Reciprocal Access Agreement signed in 2024 and brought into force on September 11, 2025, which allows the two countries to host each other's forces for training.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly's Oral GLP-1 Foundayo Shows 16% Lower Cardiovascular Risk in Landmark Diabetes Trial

key_facts.fact: Eli Lilly's Phase 3 ACHIEVE-4 trial of Foundayo (orforglipron) met its primary endpoint, demonstrating non-inferiority to insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity at high cardiovascular risk.

The risk of major cardiovascular events (MACE) was 16% lower in the Foundayo group compared to insulin. A 57% reduction in all-cause mortality was also observed, though the trial did not control for multiplicity on that endpoint.
Foundayo showed superior A1C reduction (1.6% vs 1.0%) and weight loss (8.8% vs 1.7% weight gain) compared to insulin glargine at 52 weeks, with benefits lasting through 104 weeks of treatment.

ACHIEVE-4 enrolled over 2,700 patients across 15 countries, making it Foundayo's largest and longest-running study. The trial's liver injury analysis confirmed no safety signals, addressing an FDA concern from the April 1 obesity approval.

Lilly plans to submit Foundayo to the FDA for a type 2 diabetes indication by end of Q2 2026, using the new Secretary's National Priority Review Voucher Program. Foundayo was approved for obesity on April 1.

stories.headline: Musk's TeraFab Team Contacts Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron, Lam Research for Chipmaking Gear

key_facts.fact: Staff working for the Tesla-SpaceX joint venture have sought price quotes and delivery times for chipmaking gear from Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron, and Lam Research, among others.
The TeraFab team contacted makers of photomasks, substrates, etchers, depositors, cleaning devices, testers, and other tools. Musk wants to move at 'light speed.'
Samsung proposed allocating more capacity for Tesla at its planned factory in Taylor, Texas, rather than supporting the TeraFab project directly.
The goal is to begin silicon manufacturing by 2029 and then scale up. Analysts estimate the project would require $5 trillion to $13 trillion in capital spending.
Intel has said it will join the TeraFab initiative, with CEO Lip Bu Tan posting a photo of Musk on a recent visit to the chipmaker's Santa Clara office.
Shares of Tokyo Electron closed up 5.3% in Tokyo on the news, while Applied Materials and Lam Research rose more than 2% in pre-market trading.

stories.headline: NiSource Signs Long-Term Power Deal With Alphabet, Expands Amazon Agreement for Indiana Data Centers

key_facts.fact: US utility NiSource signed a long-term energy supply agreement with a unit of Alphabet to support a large data center in northern Indiana, with power supply expected to begin in summer 2026.
NiSource also expanded its agreement with Amazon to speed up power delivery to its facilities and accelerate bill credits for households.
NIPSCO and GenCo will provide about 340 megawatts of dedicated capacity from a GenCo-owned portfolio supplemented by up to 175 megawatts of seasonal market purchases.
NiSource estimates about $1.25 billion in system-wide customer savings — roughly $90 to $115 annually per household — through its GenCo model that shields existing customers from added costs.
CEO Lloyd Yates said the savings expand on the previously announced $1 billion in customer savings from the Amazon deal.

stories.headline: OpenAI Doubles Cerebras Chip Commitment to $20B+, Gets Equity Stake Ahead of IPO

key_facts.fact: OpenAI agreed to pay Cerebras more than $20 billion over three years for servers powered by its chips, doubling the $10 billion deal struck in January for 750 MW of computing capacity.
OpenAI receives warrants for a minority stake in Cerebras that could grow to up to 10% if total spending reaches $30 billion over three years.
OpenAI also agreed to provide Cerebras about $1 billion to help fund data center development that would run OpenAI's AI products.
Cerebras plans to disclose parts of the OpenAI arrangement as soon as Friday, as it targets an IPO raising $3 billion at a ~$35 billion valuation, up from $23.1 billion previously.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is an early investor in Cerebras. The deal highlights the growing appetite for computing power for inference workloads.

stories.headline: OpenAI Agrees to Pay Cerebras $20B+ for Chips, May Get Equity Ahead of Cerebras' $35B IPO

key_facts.fact: OpenAI struck a deal to pay Cerebras more than $20 billion over three years for use of its server chips, double the amount previously associated with the deal.
OpenAI's spending on Cerebras could reach $30 billion, which could give OpenAI an equity stake in Cerebras as part of the agreement.
Cerebras is preparing to make its IPO public as soon as Friday, aiming to raise $3 billion or more at a valuation of $35 billion or higher, a 60% premium to its $22 billion February valuation.
The deal positions Cerebras as a significant alternative to Nvidia for AI chip supply, with OpenAI seeking to reduce its dependence on a single supplier.

stories.headline: OpenAI Codex Desktop Gains Mac Computer Control, In-App Browser, and 90+ New Plugins

key_facts.fact: Codex desktop app now includes a 'computer use' feature that lets agents operate Mac apps in the background — viewing the screen, clicking, and typing with their own cursor — while users continue working uninterrupted.
A built-in browser based on OpenAI's Atlas browser lets users comment directly on web page elements to give Codex precise modification instructions, initially for local web apps.
Image generation via gpt-image-1.5 is now integrated directly into Codex workflows. Over 90 new plugins ship with the update, combining skills, app integrations, and MCP servers.
Automation now supports scheduling future work and resuming multi-day tasks automatically. A memory feature remembers user preferences and past corrections across sessions.
The app has 3 million weekly users. Computer Use feature is macOS-only and not yet available in the EU. The update also adds Intel Mac support for the first time.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-Rosalind, a Purpose-Built Model for Drug Discovery and Life Sciences

key_facts.fact: GPT-Rosalind is a frontier reasoning model optimized for biology, drug discovery, and translational medicine, available as a research preview in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API for qualified enterprise customers.
Launch partners include Amgen, Moderna, the Allen Institute, and Thermo Fisher Scientific. A free Life Sciences plugin for Codex connects to over 50 scientific tools and databases.

The model tops BixBench (real bioinformatics) among models with published scores, and exceeds GPT-5.4 on 6 of 11 LABBench2 tasks. On RNA sequence prediction it reaches the 95th percentile of human experts.
Only one in 10 drugs entering clinical trials ultimately gets approved, and no fully AI-discovered drug has made it through phase 3 trials yet.
The model is named after Rosalind Franklin. It was built on top of OpenAI's newest internal models and is deployed through a trusted-access program with enterprise-grade security controls.

stories.headline: Physical Intelligence's π0.7 Shows First Signs of Compositional Generalization in Robotics

key_facts.fact: π0.7 is a steerable generalist robotic foundation model that exhibits compositional generalization — recombining skills from training data to solve tasks it was never explicitly trained on.

In an air fryer experiment, with effectively only 2 pieces of training data related to the device, π0.7 successfully cooked sweet potatoes when given step-by-step language instructions — success rate rose from 5% to 95% after 30 minutes of prompt refinement.

The model provides zero-shot cross-embodiment transfer — enabling a robot to fold laundry without any laundry-folding data — and matches the performance of specialized RL-finetuned models on dexterous tasks.

Co-founder Sergey Levine compared the emergent capabilities to early LLM scaling, saying when robots move from performing only trained tasks to combining them in new ways, 'the magnitude of performance improvement grows.'
Physical Intelligence has raised more than $1 billion to date and was recently valued at $5 billion. The researchers define π0.7 as an early signal still at research stage.

stories.headline: US Refuses to Renew Russia and Iran Oil Sanctions Waivers, Threatens Secondary Sanctions on Buyers

key_facts.fact: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on April 16 that the US will not renew the 30-day general licenses that allowed delivery of Russian and Iranian crude oil loaded before March 12. The Russian oil waiver expired April 11.

Bessent warned that the US could impose secondary sanctions on countries continuing to purchase Iranian oil, and sent letters to two Chinese banks warning of potential sanctions if Iranian funds transit through their accounts.

India had exploited the waiver to purchase around 1.98 million barrels per day of Russian oil in March 2026, up from roughly 1 mb/d in February. India was the second-highest buyer of Russian fossil fuels in March at €5.8 billion.
Physical crude oil prices have already hit near $150 per barrel. Analysts warn that cutting Russian and Iranian crude while the Hormuz disruption continues will further rile energy markets.

stories.headline: US Lawmakers Scale Back MATCH Act Chip Bill but Keep ASML DUV Sales Ban to China

key_facts.fact: The revised MATCH Act has been softened from its early April version but still introduces a nationwide restriction on ASML's deep ultraviolet (DUV) immersion lithography sales to China.
The House Foreign Affairs Committee is set to vote on the bill next Wednesday, alongside more than a dozen others related to AI, semiconductors, and export controls.
Nationwide curbs on cryogenic etch tools (produced by Lam Research and Tokyo Electron) have been removed from the revised version.

The bill still prohibits foreign firms from selling to China's leading memory makers and SMIC for facilities Washington has barred from using US tools, and requires licenses to service equipment in covered facilities.

The earlier version was described by one expert as a 'runaway train.' Dutch PM Jetten discussed the issue with Trump at a White House dinner; the Netherlands has pushed back against proposed US export limits on ASML.
